evals.name: wireup-compose-react-express-auth0
evals.prompt: Hey — we have a React frontend (Vite, port 5173) and a Node/Express API (port 4000) in this monorepo, and the whole thing runs locally via docker-compose. Right now the frontend hits our Auth0 tenant for login (see frontend/src/auth.ts) and the API verifies JWTs against Auth0's JWKS (see backend/src/jwt.ts). I'd like to swap out Auth0 for dev-oidc when running locally so I don't have to keep our shared Auth0 dev tenant alive. Set it up. Two test users would be enough — let's call them alice and bob, and please give bob a `role: admin` claim. Don't change the prod config; just make local dev go through dev-oidc.
evals.expected_output: A new dev-oidc.config.json at repo root with one client (clientId/audience/redirectUri matching what's in the app) and two profiles (alice + bob with admin claim). The config must NOT include `issuer`, `host`, or `port` — the v0.2 schema rejects them. A dev-oidc service block in docker-compose.yml or docker-compose.override.yml with the volume mount, port mapping, and healthcheck. Local-dev env variables (in .env.development or compose environment block) updated so OIDC_ISSUER/AUTHORITY points at http://localhost:8095. Production .env not modified.
expectations: dev-oidc.config.json exists at the working directory root
dev-oidc.config.json is valid JSON and parses cleanly under the v0.2 schema (no issuer/host/port fields)
config.clients[] has at least one entry whose redirectUris contains http://localhost:5173/auth/callback
config.profiles[] contains profiles with id 'alice' and id 'bob'
The 'bob' profile has a claims object with role equal to 'admin'
docker-compose.yml or docker-compose.override.yml has a service named 'dev-oidc' using a dev-oidc image
The dev-oidc service mounts dev-oidc.config.json into /config/config.json
The dev-oidc service exposes port 8095 to the host
The original .env file containing the Auth0 issuer (acme-dev.us.auth0.com) was not modified — production values are intact
A dev-only override exists (a new .env.development / .env.local file, or compose environment block changes) pointing the app's OIDC_ISSUER / VITE_OIDC_AUTHORITY at http://localhost:8095
frontend/src/auth.ts and backend/src/jwt.ts source files were not modified

evals.name: wireup-vite-msal-no-docker
evals.prompt: I'm working on a Vite SPA that uses MSAL to sign in against our Entra tenant. There's no Docker in this project and I'd like to keep it that way — the rest of the team runs `npm run dev` and that's it. Can you wire up dev-oidc as the local IdP so I can test login flows offline? My backend reads `oid` from the JWT, not `sub`, so make sure that lines up.
evals.expected_output: A dev-oidc.config.json at repo root with subjectClaim 'oid', one client matching the MSAL configuration, and a couple of profiles. The config must NOT include `issuer`, `host`, or `port`. Run mode: either dev-oidc as a devDependency with a `dev:oidc` script (legacy CLI), or README/CONTRIBUTING documents Hub setup (`dev-oidc register . && dev-oidc start`). Dev env override (.env.local or .env.development) pointing the MSAL authority at the dev-oidc URL. src/authConfig.ts updated with `knownAuthorities` and `protocolMode: 'OIDC'` (MSAL refuses to talk to non-Microsoft authorities without these). No Docker artifacts introduced.
expectations: dev-oidc.config.json exists at the working directory root
dev-oidc.config.json is valid JSON and parses cleanly under the v0.2 schema (no issuer/host/port fields)
config.subjectClaim equals 'oid' (required for Entra/MSAL compatibility)
config.clients[] has at least one entry with a redirectUri matching http://localhost:5173/auth/callback
config.profiles[] has at least 2 profiles

Run mode wired: either package.json declares dev-oidc devDependency + a script that runs `dev-oidc start --config ...`, or README/CONTRIBUTING documents Hub setup with `dev-oidc register` and `dev-oidc start`
No docker-compose.yml or Dockerfile was created in the working directory
The original .env file (containing VITE_AZURE_AUTHORITY pointing at login.microsoftonline.com) was not modified
A dev-only override exists (e.g. .env.local or .env.development) pointing VITE_AZURE_AUTHORITY at the dev-oidc URL (http://localhost:8095 or http://localhost:8095/<slug>)
src/authConfig.ts has been updated to set `protocolMode: 'OIDC'` and add `knownAuthorities` containing the dev-oidc host (MSAL fails against non-Microsoft authorities without these)
src/main.tsx was not modified

evals.name: edit-add-client-profile-persist-key
evals.prompt: We already have dev-oidc running fine for the main app. Two changes: (1) my teammate is building a separate admin portal at http://localhost:5180 — it needs its own client called `admin-portal` with audience `admin-api`, and it should require a client secret since it has a backend. (2) I'm getting tired of re-logging-in every time I rebuild the dev-oidc container — please make the signing key persistent. (3) Also add a profile `support-agent` (email support@acme.dev) with a claim `role: support` so we can test that user type.
evals.expected_output: Existing dev-oidc.config.json edited in place: a second client with clientId 'admin-portal', a clientSecret, redirectUris on http://localhost:5180, audience 'admin-api'. signingKey.source changed from 'generate' to 'file:<path>'. Compose file gets a /data volume mount paired with the keyfile path. New profile 'support-agent' with the requested email and role: support claim. No unrelated edits, and no introduction of issuer/host/port (which the v0.2 schema rejects).
expectations: dev-oidc.config.json clients[] has exactly 2 entries (was 1)
There is a client with clientId 'admin-portal'
The 'admin-portal' client has audience 'admin-api'
The 'admin-portal' client has a non-empty clientSecret field
The 'admin-portal' client has at least one redirectUri starting with 'http://localhost:5180'
The original 'main-app' client is still present with its original clientId, redirectUris, and audience unchanged
signingKey.source starts with 'file:' (no longer 'generate')
docker-compose.yml has a volume mount on the dev-oidc service that backs the signing key path (typically a /data mount) — paired with either a named volume definition or a host bind mount
profiles[] has exactly 3 entries (was 2)
There is a profile with id 'support-agent'
The 'support-agent' profile has email 'support@acme.dev'
The 'support-agent' profile has a claims object with role equal to 'support'
The original 'alice' and 'bob' profiles are still present and unchanged
The edited config still contains no `issuer`, `host`, or `port` fields (rejected by v0.2 schema)
